step_by_step_reasoning: Nodes: two client actors (tenant/customer web-mobile client, and third-party reseller/OTA API client), CDN (ThirdParty), S3 static hosting, AppSync GraphQL gateway, API Gateway REST endpoint, a single fused Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB. Flow 0: tenant onboarding wizard: client -> CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda -> SQS fan-out -> Lambda reprocess -> DynamoDB. Flow 1: reseller/OTA: API client -> CDN -> API Gateway -> same Lambda -> DynamoDB. Flow 2: customer website: client -> CDN -> S3 static content, returned to client; dynamic content CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda or direct DynamoDB resolvers. Flow 3: check-in via mobile app: client -> CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda <-> DynamoDB, Lambda -> SQS -> Lambda for post-experience processing (review reminder email). Email service is not named or drawn, so no node is added.

graph.name: Anchor: Multi-Tenant Serverless Ticketing Platform
graph.notes: Anchor is a ticketing platform with more than 40 tenants (20+ onboarded in the last six months) serving daytime experiences such as Statue of Liberty cruises, Niagara Falls, Alcatraz Island and NYC Ferry. Fully serverless: CDN in front of S3 static hosting, AppSync GraphQL and API Gateway REST, shared Lambda functions, SQS for fan-out and deferred processing, and DynamoDB with shared tables partitioned by tenant.

nodes.name: Tenant / Customer Client (Web & Mobile App)
nodes.notes: Tenants using the onboarding wizard web application, customers buying via owned websites or mobile app, and the mobile check-in application used to look up bookings or scan tickets.

nodes.name: Third-Party Reseller / OTA
nodes.notes: Omni-channel resellers (OTAs) such as Expedia, Viator and GetYourGuide selling the offerings through a third-party API implemented for them.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.notes: First thing every client request hits. Returns static content from S3 to the client and routes dynamic requests to AppSync or API Gateway.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Bucket serving as an HTTP server hosting static content: event/ticket offering descriptions and pictures.

nodes.name: AppSync
nodes.notes: GraphQL gateway. Resolvers invoke Lambda; sometimes direct DynamoDB resolvers are used, mapped and reused via built-in pipeline resolvers.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Regular REST endpoint for the third-party API used by resellers/OTAs; hits the same Lambdas as the other channels.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Shared functions for tenants and customers, triggered through AppSync and API Gateway. Fans out to subroutines by sending SQS messages, later reprocesses those messages, and interacts with DynamoDB.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Holds fan-out messages for tenant setup and messages for anything after check-in (customer service, post-experience, review reminder email), later processed by Lambda.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores all tenant data. Multi-tenancy: tables are shared, with a partition key per tenant so everything is partitioned by tenant.

edges.notes: Tenant uses the onboarding wizard web application; the request first hits the CDN.
CDN forwards the request to AppSync, the GraphQL gateway.
AppSync resolvers tell Lambda to fan out to different subroutines.
Lambda sends a bunch of SQS messages for the fan-out.
SQS messages are later reprocessed by Lambda.
Lambda interacts with DynamoDB to finish setting up the tenancy, partitioned by tenant key.
Reseller/OTA request first hits the CDN.
CDN routes the reseller request to the REST third-party API on API Gateway.
API Gateway hits the same Lambdas used by the other channels.
Lambda reads/writes booking data in DynamoDB.
Customer starts the journey on an owned website; request hits the CDN.
CDN requests the static offering content from the S3 bucket acting as HTTP server.
S3 returns event descriptions and pictures to the CDN.
CDN returns the static content to the client, who can browse and navigate.
For dynamic content the CDN hits AppSync (GraphQL).
AppSync takes a node of the graph and processes it using Lambda.
Sometimes straight DynamoDB resolvers are used, mapped and reused with AppSync pipeline resolvers.
Lambda reads/writes data in DynamoDB.
Mobile check-in application looks up the booking or scans the ticket; request goes through the CDN.
Same flow: CDN forwards to AppSync.
AppSync invokes Lambda for the check-in.
Lambda writes the check-in to DynamoDB.
DynamoDB returns booking data to Lambda (bidirectional interaction).
Lambda puts messages in SQS for anything after check-in: customer service, post-experience.
Messages are later processed by Lambda; an email is sent to the customer reminding them to write a review.
